title: Sensible defaults and patterns for SDK retries, idempotency, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Lena Park
description:
Objective: Define language-consistent, safe defaults and guidance for SDK retry/backoff policies, idempotency key usage, and streaming ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Deliverables: (1) Default retry/backoff parameters and language APIs, (2) Idempotency header convention and SDK ergonomics, (3) Retryable error taxonomy, (4) Streaming resume / dedup semantics and examples, (5) Sample integration tests and PR templates.

Background and motivation: Teams repeatedly implement ad-hoc retry logic across SDKs. Inconsistent defaults lead to surprising duplicate side effects for non-idempotent endpoints or insufficient retries for transient infra errors. Streaming introduces additional complexity: reconnects can cause partial outputs, and naive retries are unsafe. We need a single canonical taxonomy and pragmatic SDK behaviors so application authors get predictable reliability without footguns.

Proposed high-level decisions (consensus goal):
- Define an explicit Idempotency-Key header and SDK-managed invocation id to enable safe retries and server-side dedup. Header name: "Idempotency-Key" (prefer standard casing) and SDK-emitted "X-Redwood-SDK-Invocation" for tracing. Generate UUIDv4 by default when SDK marks a call idempotent.
- Default retry policy for idempotent requests: max_retries=3, initial_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=2000ms, multiplier=2.0, full jitter. For low-latency use-cases (embeddings) provide an alternate preset: max_retries=2, initial_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=800ms.
- Default for non-idempotent requests: do not perform automatic body-level retries. Only allow connection-level reconnects that do NOT re-send user input unless the caller explicitly marks the request idempotent.
- Retryable error set: network errors (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, EHOSTUNREACH), HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504, gRPC UNAVAILABLE (14), gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (4). 5xx generally retryable except 501. 4xx are not retryable except 429; 409 (conflict) is considered non-retryable unless paired with an idempotency key and server contract.
- Streaming semantics: SDKs should avoid automatically re-sending stream payloads. Instead provide an opt-in streaming-resume mechanism: the client opens streams with an Idempotency-Key and optional client-side sequence offset (X-Redwood-Stream-Resume-Offset). The server can accept resume requests for a reasonable time window and return the offset accepted. SDKs expose a streaming helper that buffers sent chunks (bounded by memory limit) and uses the resume offset to continue where left off. Default streaming behavior is: no automatic body retry; automatic connection retry up to 2 attempts for transient transport failures, but only if the server indicates resume support.

Language-specific ergonomics (recommended):
- Python SDK:
  - API: client.generate(..., idempotency=True/False) and RequestOptions(idempotency_key=...)
  - Default behavior: if idempotency=True, SDK will attach Idempotency-Key header and enable full retry preset. SDK will also expose a context manager for streaming that returns a resume token and a short utility to persist it.
  - Example default config: {max_retries:3, initial_backoff_ms:200, max_backoff_ms:2000, multiplier:2.0, jitter:"full"}.

- TypeScript SDK:
  - API: client.create({..., idempotent: true}) or client.stream(...).withResume({enabled:true})
  - Default: set header "Idempotency-Key" automatically when idempotent flag true. Expose hook to provide custom generator for keys. Streaming helpers return an AsyncIterable and a resume token object.

- Go SDK:
  - API: type RequestOptions struct { IdempotencyKey string; Idempotent bool } and client.Create(ctx, req, opts)
  - Default: if opts.Idempotent true or opts.IdempotencyKey non-empty, SDK uses retry preset. Provide low-level TransportRetry hook for infra teams.

Retryable error taxonomy (user-facing shorthand):
- Transient network: ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE, ENETUNREACH -> retry
- Transport-level (HTTP/gRPC): HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504; gRPC UNAVAILABLE (14), DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (4) -> retry
- Short-circuit (do not retry): HTTP 400-499 except 429; 409 conflict -> require idempotency to retry
- Permanent server errors: HTTP 501 -> do not retry
- Streaming-specific: partial frame errors where connection closed mid-stream -> use resume protocol (if supported); otherwise surface error and do not auto-retry body.

Server contract notes (requirements to fully enable SDK behavior):
- Server must accept and store Idempotency-Key for at least 24 hours for typical requests and optionally longer for long-running batch jobs.
- Servers should implement a resume window (e.g., 60s–5m) that allows a reopened stream to continue from a client-provided offset when Idempotency-Key present.

Compatibility and migration plan:
- Roll out defaults in canary SDK builds for Python first (more tolerant ecosystem). Collect telemetry: retry rate, duplicate acceptance rate, idempotency header prevalence.
- Provide opt-out switches: set global.NO_AUTO_RETRIES or client-level config to disable automatic idempotency/auto-attach.
- Update docs with migration notes and sample code patterns.

Security/observability: SDKs should log (at debug) Idempotency-Key and invocation id (never logs PII), and surface reasons for non-retry decisions in diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implemented default retry/backoff presets in Python/TS/Go SDKs and covered by unit/integration tests.
- Streaming resume helper implemented in at least Python and TS with server-side resume contract verified in staging.
- Documentation and example snippets published in SDK docs and internal runbook.

Open questions: what server-side retention window should we require (24h vs 7d) for enterprise workloads? What memory bounds do we put on client-side buffering for stream resume?

2026-03-05: Telemetry plan: record retry_count, last_error_class, idempotency_key_present boolean. PM wants sample dashboard for release gating.
